key_insight: A physics-grounded welding digital twin combines thermal simulation, Gaussian-process surrogates, and robotic control to screen in-space joining strategies before physical testing.
engineering_relevance: Fast surrogate predictions could help tune robotic welding as travel speed changes, reducing process-development risk for future on-orbit construction and repair.
method: Finite-volume thermal model includes phase change, effective thermocapillary transport, and local pressure; gravity is assessed separately.
Gaussian-process and neural-network surrogates are compared using repeated five-fold cross-validation.
A simulated six-axis UR5 adjusts the power-source setting along an L-shaped seam.
evidence_signal: The GP outperformed the neural network on all eight outputs; finite-volume re-evaluation placed 12/12 closed-loop versus 9/12 open-loop points within an illustrative 1–3 mm root-side-width band.
watch_item: Results are simulation-based; thermal-vacuum, reduced-gravity, and robotic hardware-in-the-loop validation are still needed.
paper_title: De-Risking Robotic Welding for In-Space Metal Joining Through Physics-Grounded Digital Twins
